_note: FSC (Fantasy Stock Exchange / Flock Fantasy) 2026 WR VALUE study, transcribed from the YouTube video below. NOT a ranked board — no full 1-N order is ever stated. He groups WRs into ADP tiers (WR1-9, 10-18, 19-27, 28-36) and runs each through a point system (+5 green/best, +3 yellow, -1 orange, -3 red per league-winning signal: team pass offense rank, QB PFF grade, team pass volume, target competition, O-line rank, WR talent/YPRR, reception-perception win rate, archetype) but only calls out the actual point totals for a handful of standout players — most entries below carry his qualitative reasoning, not a score. Entries deliberately have no 'posRank' — they cast zero vote in the board's consensus rank, they only add reasoning to the research prompt. Absence from this file means not discussed in this video, not a low rank.
_source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ab5onnfGLb0 — 'I Found the Next WR League Winners (+ WR Strategy!)' (Fantasy Stock Exchange / Flock Fantasy, Aug 2026). Same channel/creator as draft-guide-fsc-archetypes.json (RB study); this is the WR video from the same series.
_confidence: Captured from captions only (--detail transcript, no frames) — the on-screen heat map with every player's exact point score was never read, only the totals he spoke aloud. 'Terrace Marshall Jr. McMillan' in captions is transcription noise for Tetairoa McMillan (rookie Panthers WR, discussed alongside Bryce Young) — mapped with high confidence, not dropped. 'Marvin Mims Jr.' mentioned only in a one-line scoring aside; kept as stated.

ja'marr chase.note: Scores highest alongside Puka Nacua. Elite talent, elite offense, elite pass volume. Only knocks: Bengals O-line, Tee Higgins will still take 100+ targets. Excluded from his top-3 '20ppg' picks as 'too obvious'.

puka nacua.note: Scores highest alongside Chase. Good-not-excellent O-line, Davante Adams likely 100+ targets, a bit more injury risk than Chase. Excluded from his top-3 '20ppg' picks as 'too obvious' — he was early on Nacua last year and it hit.

amon-ra st. brown.note: Tied for next-highest tier with JSN and Jefferson. His #1 pick for the guys you need in rounds 1-3 to find a 20ppg WR: elite team/offense/schedule, dome games, durable, always a WR1 — 'if you have no idea what you're doing, take Amon-Ra, you won't be sorry.'

jaxon smith-njigba.note: Tied for next-highest tier with St. Brown and Jefferson. Good offense but not elite; Seahawks projected more run-heavy than Rams/Bengals.

justin jefferson.note: Tied for next-highest tier. More target competition than in past years (Jennings, Addison, Hockenson) plus real QB downgrade risk with Kyler Murray after a rough 2025 that showed he's 'not QB-proof.'

nico collins.note: Scores over 30 (his 2nd-tier group). One of his 3 picks for a 20ppg WR: clear #1 target, high YPRR, prior WR1 finish. Knock: Texans O-line is one of the league's worst, some target competition from Dell/Higgins/Noel/Schultz.

devonta smith.note: Scores over 30. One of his 3 picks for a 20ppg WR: now the clear WR1 in Philly with Hurts/Kellen Moore scheme upside; was 'every bit as good as A.J. Brown' as a WR2.

george pickens.note: Scores over 30. Same green flags as CeeDee Lamb (great offense/QB/pass volume) but a notch below on injury durability and target share ceiling; still a prime WR1 archetype.

zay flowers.note: Scores over 30. Played like an 18+ ppg receiver in 2025 despite a bad QB/offense; new OC (Doyle, from the Ben Johnson tree) projects a league-average pass rate, a big upgrade for a Ravens offense that's been one of the league's slowest/most run-heavy. Bull case tied to Lamar bouncing back.

garrett wilson.note: Scores over 20 despite sitting outside the top-2 ADP tiers — notably positive given his lower price. Talent alone can get him to WR1 production, but the Jets' offensive competence (Frank Reich, Aaron Glenn) and pass volume are the concern, not Geno Smith specifically (he views Geno as an actual downgrade from Rodgers, not the reason for optimism).

jaylen waddle.note: His single biggest winner of the whole exercise — scores MORE than Lamb, Drake London, A.J. Brown and others going well ahead of him in ADP. Now Denver's clear #1 (first time since Tyreek left Miami), prime-WR1 archetype, offensive line graded #1 in the league by Football Outsiders/FTN/Sharp/Mike Clay, Bo Nix called an underrated/sneaky-MVP QB, Broncos threw 612 times last year. His pick for 'this year's JSN' — the true league-winner value play since he goes ~round 4. Ethan flagged this as a favorite call from the video.

terry mclaurin.note: Worries this is a 'trusty veteran' archetype on a shaky O-line and a team with no proven WR2/3/4 or TE; bull case is pure volume if Washington's offense holds (Jayden Daniels + McLaurin would be nearly the whole passing game), bear case is the offense regresses toward 2025 form rather than the 2024 breakout.

luther burden iii.note: Good breakout-candidate profile (good offense, good QB expected) but target competition from Loveland and Odunze (both projected 100+ targets) and simply unproven — compares him to Xavier Worthy as a hyped rookie breakout who didn't convert.

mike evans.note: TD upside boosted by the Ricky Pearsall injury, but he's a 'trusty veteran' archetype (bust-prone in mid rounds) and has his own injury risk; likes Davante Adams better at a similar career stage because he trusts the Rams offense/Stafford/McVay scheme over the 49ers'.

davante adams.note: Prefers him over Mike Evans at a similar career stage — trusts the Rams' pass volume/pace and McVay's scheme more than the 49ers', which is why Adams got 14 TDs last year.

jameson williams.note: Won't get 20ppg volume unless Amon-Ra goes down (as happened late 2025), but the Lions offense buoys him as the #2 — 'discount version of George Pickens/Tee Higgins.'

dj moore.note: Good offensive situation (Josh Allen, good O-line) but over 29 and hasn't matched his 2023 (Justin Fields, Chicago) level since — could smash on situation alone, but recent play makes that a bit surprising to bet on.

christian watson.note: Scores well in the WR28-36 tier. Good volume, good 2025 breakout, prime-WR2 archetype (finishes as a WR2), projects as Green Bay's #1 receiver on a solid offense.

tetairoa mcmillan.note: Rookie WR19 on Underdog for the Panthers. Good rookie season to build on, but offense/QB (Bryce Young) is the swing factor — a good-not-great pick at cost unless Young keeps trending positively, in which case he'd move up to his WR15-20 range.

rome odunze.note: Scores #2 in the WR28-36 tier. His preference over Luther Burden — had a 10-week stretch producing like a WR1 pre-injury as a former top-10 pick, no lingering injury concern (Odunze himself says he feels fine), and 'somehow the cheapest pass-catcher on his own team.' One of his 3 picks for a mid-round Olave/Pickens-type league winner.

brian thomas jr..note: The only player in green in the WR28-36 tier — his top pick for this year's Olave/Pickens-type mid-round league winner. Was a WR1 before at 24 years old, plays for a good team/offense that projects to pass a lot; the only real knocks are a bad 2025 (played hurt) and target competition from other mouths in the offense.

jordan addison.note: Comped to Tetairoa McMillan — unproven rookie-adjacent uncertainty, but in an up-tempo pass-heavy offense; would need a Chris Olave injury to have a league-winning ceiling of his own.

parker washington.note: Good offensive situation and camp buzz but no real track record yet; thinks he's currently overrated relative to Brian Thomas Jr. going right next to him in ADP — BTJ should go a round or two ahead.

marvin harrison jr..note: Bull case: plays in a pass-heavy offense that's fed him TD volume before, and per Matt Harmon's reception-perception data he graded 80th percentile vs. man/press coverage even in a rough rookie year — his issue was finding soft spots vs. zone, which experience should fix. Scored lower in the WR28-36 tier's point exercise than Michael Wilson, but the analyst says he personally likes MHJ's ceiling better anyway.

makai lemon.note: One of his favorite mid-round breakout picks — good prospect profile fits a Sean McVay/Shanahan-style scheme well behind a good O-line on an Eagles offense he expects to be good and more pass-heavy.

quentin johnston.note: Similar profile to Ladd McConkey (great offense/QB, likes the McDaniel scheme) but likely gets out-targeted by McConkey and lacks McConkey's 2-year track record of WR1-level production; likes him at current cost anyway.

michael wilson.note: Scored higher than Marvin Harrison Jr. in his WR28-36 point exercise and was a WR1 producer down the stretch in 2025 — flagged as a name this exercise made him want to draft more of, though he says MHJ's ceiling is still higher in his personal view.

michael pittman jr..note: One of his 3 picks for a mid-round Olave/Pickens-type league winner. Was a fringe WR1 before (WR13 in ppg at his peak); good fit as a quick-strike PPR chain-mover for Aaron Rodgers.

chris godwin jr..note: Likes him to bounce back — has posted 15ppg-level production in seasons Mike Evans has missed time, even before his own early-career peak.

courtland sutton.note: Views as a good #2 in Denver, but thinks Waddle is clearly better and Sutton likely lacks real league-winning ceiling absent a Waddle injury.

ladd mcconkey.note: Very good projection — likes the Chargers offense/Herbert with McDaniel arriving, but isn't fully convinced McConkey gets a dominant (28-30%) target share over Quentin Johnston; more likely a 25/22 split in his view. Still a good bet if you believe he can command 10+ targets/7ish catches a game; noted as still a 'breakout candidate' archetype (year 3, not yet a proven WR1).

emeka egbuka.note: Clean situational projection (good O-line, offense he expects to bounce back) but a 'breakout candidate' archetype, not yet a proven WR1 — played like a true WR1 for his first 7-8 games in 2025 before an injury-marred fade (Baker Mayfield/Bucky Irving both got hurt); an honorable mention for this year's JSN-type breakout.

malik nabers.note: Elite talent (dominant target share, top YPRR/reception-perception) but two real concerns: a knee injury recovery, and John Harbaugh's arrival likely pushing the Giants more run-heavy than under Brian Daboll — an honorable mention for this year's JSN-type breakout despite the elite ability.
